answer: New agents begin with spending limits, and counterparties raise them only after the agent completes jobs that are independently verified and backed by escrow. A Sybil farm can mint identities cheaply, but each one must lock scarce funds and pay real costs to build a trustworthy signal; splitting work across accounts does not transfer a good history. The tide of new identities therefore cannot instantly buy influence: an attacker must tie up capital and repeatedly deliver useful work on every account, making a broad voyage of fake agents costly and slow.
